fx.fx_commentary: The Canadian dollar closed at 0.7198 USD/CAD on March 31, declining 1.85% month-over-month to a two-month low as geopolitical uncertainty drove safe-haven demand for the US dollar.1 The USD/CAD rate moved to 1.3893, reflecting a widening differential between the Bank of Canada's overnight rate of 2.25% and the US Federal Reserve's target rate of 4.25-4.50% — a spread of approximately 200-225 basis points favoring the US dollar.23 The euro strengthened to 1.1460 against the US dollar as European markets repriced geopolitical risk premiums; this EUR/USD level reflects a divergence between the ECB's rate path and US monetary policy expectations.4 If the CAD/USD rate holds near 0.72, the database's 49 export-exposed manufacturing projects would face elevated input cost pressure from US dollar-denominated material costs, while energy exporters would see higher CAD-denominated revenues from US-dollar-priced crude.5

yieldCurve.yield_commentary: The Government of Canada yield curve maintained a normal (upward-sloping) shape through the week of March 24-30, with the 2-year/10-year spread at 63 basis points — wider than the 60 basis point spread recorded a year ago.6 The 2-year yield closed at 2.95%, up 33 basis points from 2.62% a year ago, while the 10-year yield closed at 3.58%, up 36 basis points from 3.22% a year ago, reflecting higher term premiums associated with elevated federal government debt issuance and geopolitical uncertainty.7 The 30-year yield closed at 3.94%, up 41 basis points from 3.53% a year ago. If the current long-end yield environment persists, the database's 1,034 under-construction projects — which depend on long-term financing rates for project completion — would face funding costs at the higher end of their feasibility study assumptions.8
